title: PrefixCache silent-corruption investigation, detection hooks, and cleanup sweep
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a production capacity event on 2025-03-09 we observed sporadic request responses that contained stale or unexpectedly truncated output when the request path hit the prefix cache. Unlike a pure eviction or out-of-memory event, affected entries sometimes returned silently corrupted payloads (missing trailing tokens or mismatched metadata) rather than errors. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate mitigations deployed, and follow-up hardening and observability work to detect and prevent silent corruption in the prefix/KV cache.

Impact: Intermittent incorrect responses for small percentage of requests (estimated 0.6% for a 3-hour window). No customer data exfiltration. Primary risk: customer-facing model output incorrectness and downstream business logic misbehavior.

Observed signals and timeline: 2025-03-09 02:12 UTC — anomaly alert from request validation pipeline: checksum mismatch on structured response schema. 2025-03-09 02:18 UTC — spike in internal metric prefixcache.unexpected_hit_version and increased rpc-retries to backend model. 2025-03-09 02:45 UTC — first on-call investigation linked to autoscaler burst and concurrent cache compaction job. 2025-03-10 — initial mitigations deployed (see updates).

Root cause (conclusion of investigation): A race between the asynchronous compaction/eviction worker and a new fast-path prefix write introduced in runtime-1.20. The fast-path bypassed a small atomic sequence-number update; under high concurrency and bursty eviction, a partial write could persist a payload with an older header but newer body (or vice versa), producing structurally inconsistent entries that are valid bytes but semantically corrupt. The compaction code assumed last-write-wins based on a per-entry timestamp but there was a clock skew edge-case where simultaneous writes from different workers used slightly different monotonic references.

Why this differed from prior eviction incidents: This produced valid cache hits (so no cache-miss telemetry) and did not throw memory errors; it was a data-integrity issue, not a capacity or reference-count leak. Existing telemetry tracked evictions and OOMs but not per-entry integrity checks, so the condition went unnoticed until surface-level schema validation flagged a malformed response.

Immediate mitigations applied (already deployed): - Temporarily disabled the fast-path write in runtime-1.20; reverted to the atomic write path (hotfix: PR #1823). - Added conservative serialization-level checks that assert header/body coordinate (deployed to hosted control plane only) and return cache-miss on mismatch to prevent serving corrupt payloads. - Rate-limited parallel compaction jobs during peak autoscaler events to reduce racing windows.

Longer-term actions (tracked below as discrete action items): - Add per-entry 64-bit checksum and version tag to every prefixcache entry; verify checksum on each read and log example payloads when checksum fails. - Introduce monotonic write sequence numbers stored in a WAL for each cache shard to provide atomic compare-and-swap semantics for writes. - Improve compaction job to consult sequence numbers rather than timestamps; make compaction idempotent. - Extend integration test harness with synthetic bursty workloads and a fault injector that simulates partial writes and clock skew. - Add telemetry and alerts: prefixcache.checksum_failures (counter), prefixcache.ttl_drift_p50/p95 (histograms), prefixcache.unexpected_structure_rate (rate), and an SLO that alerts on >0 checksum failures for 5 minutes in production. - Backfill a light-weight scan job to detect and incrementally repair corrupt entries in non-critical regions. - Update rollout playbook: any change to fast-path writes requires a local chaos test and canary in prod with structured-output verification.

Verification criteria: zero checksum failure alerts in canary tier during a 24h window and automated synthetic workload run showing no structural inconsistencies across 10M simulated requests.

Owner: Daniel Kim. Secondary reviewer: Priya Nair.
updates: 2025-03-10: Hotfix deployed (runtime PR #1823) that disables fast-path prefix writes and forces atomic writer; immediate drop in corruption signals observed. — Daniel Kim
2025-03-11: Added temporary read-time guard that turns corrupt hits into cache-misses; phased deploy across regions. Reduced customer-facing incorrectness to near-zero. — SRE team

2025-03-12: Initial draft of checksum/version design doc posted (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/PrefixCache+Checksum+Design). Added metric names and alert thresholds. — Daniel Kim

2025-03-14: Implemented and tested per-entry checksum proto in unit tests; found a serialization edge-case during deserialization of older entries. Filed follow-up task ENG-11003 to handle on-disk upgrade path. — Aisha Patel

2025-03-16: Began integration test harness work; added fault-injection that simulates write truncation and clock skew. Early runs found a secondary race in garbage collection; mitigation planned. — Integration team
2025-03-18: Canary plan approved. Will run checksum-enabled canary on 2 dedicated nodes for 48h before wider rollout. — Program management
comments: Priya Nair (PM): Please prioritize telemetry and alerting so we detect regressions before customer reports. Keep me posted on canary results.
Carlos Alvarez (SRE): We need retention controls for sampled corrupt payloads to avoid PII exposure in logs; added policy note to design doc.
Martin Zhou (Eng): Good catch on the older-entry deserialization; we should include a migration path that converts entries lazily on read rather than a blocking offline migration.
Sarah Lopez (Security): Confirmed no customer data exfiltration; review of sample logs required before sharing with external stakeholders.
Lead Eng Review (2025-03-15): Recommend adding a small stochastic delay on compaction jobs to further reduce synchronized races across shards.
action_items: AI-1: Implement per-entry checksum and version tag, server-side verification on read (owner: Daniel Kim, estimate: 3)
AI-2: Add WAL-backed monotonic sequence numbers for writes and update compaction to use sequence compare (owner: Martin Zhou, estimate: 5)
AI-3: Extend integration harness with write-truncation and clock-skew fault injector; include automated verification Check (owner: Integration team, estimate: 3)
AI-4: Create telemetry dashboards and alert rules for checksum failures and unexpected-structure-rate (owner: Observability team, estimate: 2)
AI-5: Implement lazy on-read migration for older entries and a short-term repair sweep to fix corrupted entries in non-critical shards (owner: Storage team, estimate: 4)
AI-6: Update rollout playbook to require chaos and structured-output canary for all fast-path write changes (owner: Program management, due: 2025-03-25)
AI-7: Security review of sampled payload logging and retention policy (owner: Security, due: 2025-03-22)
